system.summary: Homophonic alphabet of symbols (a-m) and digits 2-10 marked bare/dot/colon (n-p, r-s, t-u-y), dotted-letter word codes, about 30 name symbols and a list of null words (English ports, 'and', 'bycause').

diacritics.note: Dot vs colon after a digit changes its letter; dots/colons/bars around a Latin letter select the code word.

system.sibling_key: Throckmorton's and Croft's ciphers are filed with it (R9260, R9262, R9261 p.2); not used.
system.notes: Key: Add MS 4136 f. 179 'Sr Thomas Smith's Cipher' (DECODE R9261 p.1), Forbes's copy. 'enos' is Ambassador, not a null.

prior_solution.where: Contemporary decipherments on the SP 70 originals; 1562/3 letters printed in full by Forbes, A Full View (1740-41); later letters summarised in CSP Foreign vols 6-8 (1869-71)

conditions.human_role: Supplied the DECODE login cookie (earlier session); set the target.

solution.what: Fetched DECODE R9248-R9254 images and key record R9262 with the saved cookie.
R9262 is Throckmorton's cipher, not Smith's; the API listing of neighbouring key records found R9261, 'Sr Thomas Smith's Cipher' (f. 179).
Applied the key to 17 Jan 1562/3 passages: 'chief ... side' read at once.
CSP Foreign vol. 6 no. 109 cites Forbes ii 287; Forbes vol. 2 OCR on archive.org prints the letter; the reading matches. Add MS 4136 identified as Forbes's deciphering file.
Transcribed and read the 1564 Arles 24 Nov passage from the glyphs; matches the CSP no. 815 summary.
First parallel agent on the 1564-65 letters read only parts of two letters.
Agents read R9249 and R9250 letters (27 Jan and 13 Apr 1563 in full, 1563/4-1566 in part) and the 1564-65 letters in R9252-R9254 (most in large part), checking against Forbes and CSP.
Readings agree with Forbes's printed text and CSP summaries; two date corrections (Avignon 4 Oct not 27 Oct 1564; 22 Mar 1565/6 not 1566/7).
R9236 (f.140) fetched from DECODE; five letters' cipher passages on one leaf, nulls London/Lyn/Poole/Dover/Hastings/Garnesey identify Smith's key.
Two agents deciphered the passages sign by sign with key R9261; new variant: double bar = i.
15 Oct and 15/17 Dec 1562 agree with Forbes ii 119 and 238; 20 Oct 1562, 4 Nov 1563 and 31 Jan 1562/3 not found in Forbes, read from glyphs only.

Located 20 Oct 1562 in Forbes ii 122 (CSP F. 5 no. 880) and 4 Nov 1563 in CSP F. 6 no. 1366; resolved 'garden'/'side'/'chamillion' and 'La Rochelle'. 31 Jan 1562/3 advertisements not found in print; only (2) 'queen of Navarre' read.

31 Jan 1562/3 advertisements: searched CSP F. 6 (21 Jan-10 Feb 1563) and Forbes ii Jan-Feb 1563; no printed text. Full-resolution re-read gives only '(1) Monsieur de [L]uy', '(2) the queen of Navarre', last line '… band that [K. of Navarre/Fr. King] and …'; CSP has 'the Queen of Navarre's band' in Warwick's news of late Jan 1563 as context only.

Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): decipher_A-E.md (glyphs and plaintext per passage) mapped to 21 of the 23 letters; nos. 01 (17 Jan 1562/3, spot-read) and 04 (12 Mar 1562/3, not transcribed, printed in Forbes) have no files; key KEY.md

Reading audit (George Lasry's sentence test, 22 Oct 2026): decipher_A-E.md read letter by letter. Nos. 02, 07, 10, 12, 14 and 21 read as English sentences or as passages that build them with the printed text (reviewed B); the other fifteen transcribed letters are isolated names, code items and fragments, and nos. 01 and 04 are not transcribed: relabelled decoded, not read. Class read -> read in part; fraction_read unknown -> ~0.45 (estimated by passages).

Re-read under REREAD_BRIEF (batch b03): DECODE R9236 image fetched with the project cookie (the other records were in the main checkout); Forbes, A Full View ii page images fetched from archive.org (leaves 151, 155, 353-355, 416-425, 450-452), since the OCR garbles lines.

Found that Forbes sets every deciphered word in italic; the cipher passages of nos. 01, 03, 04, 05, 19, 20 align one to one with the italic stretches and were checked on the glyphs (01 all 13; 04 passages 1-24 and spot checks on f. 168). Nos. 01 and 04, never transcribed, now read from the print aligned with the figures.

Nos. 06, 08, 11, 13, 15-18, 22, 23 re-read passage by passage on full-resolution crops with key R9261; label corrections in no01-no23_corrections.tsv. Values that hold across documents: m̄ = marriage (nos. 11, 13, 15), ·∂ = sea (nos. 11, 15), ‖ = i on ff. 140/159; M̈ = my in no. 03 (my or marry in no. 08); key-sheet words checked on R9261 p. 1 (secret, crown, carry, came, king, overmuch, privy, she, woman, whom).

Readings and English written for 16 letters (no<NN>_reading.md, _en.md); _check_reading.py clean share 0.50-1.0 (15 lowest: short sentences with one hole). State decoded, not read -> read for nos. 01, 03, 04, 05, 06, 08, 09, 11, 13, 15, 16, 17, 18, 19, 20, 22; fraction_read ~0.45 -> ~0.99 (estimated by passages).

No. 23 (advertisements from France, 31 Jan 1562/3) re-read on the image: only "Monsieur de [?]uy" and "the queen of Navarre" read; not in Forbes or CSP Foreign vi, signs not in the key, each once. Left decoded, not read.

outcome.method_basis: The key is filed in the same manuscript as the letters: DECODE R9261 p. 1 = Add MS 4136 f. 179, 'Sr Thomas Smith's Cipher', in Forbes's deciphering file; the readings were checked against Forbes's A Full View (1740-41) and CSP Foreign.
outcome.notes: Most passages read; code signs in the hooked-T family read from context. 22 Oct 2026, re-read (batch b03): nos. 01 and 04 aligned with Forbes's italics (Forbes prints the deciphered words in italic) and read; nos. 03, 05, 19, 20 read in their printed sentences; nos. 06, 08, 09, 11, 13, 15-18, 22 re-read on the images (m̄ = marriage, ·∂ = sea, ‖ = i, key-sheet words checked on R9261) and read as the passages themselves, set by the CSP calendar. No. 23 (advertisements, 31 Jan 1562/3) stays decoded, not read: no clear text, unknown signs once each. Single unread signs remain in nos. 08, 11, 15, 16, 17, 18 (no01-no23_reread_log.md).

texts.label: No. 01, Smith to the Queen, Chartres, 17 Jan 1562/3 (R9248, f. 157)
texts.summary: Smith to the Queen, Chartres, 17 Jan 1562/3 (Forbes ii 287-289): someone should be sent to the Admiral, now chief on the other side, and Mr Middlemore would be fit; the Guisians will make no agreement with the Queen; the Constable suspects the Guise and fears the ruin of the Châtillons; if the Admiral holds out, necessity will force an accord; the Queen should act with speed while the Huguenot faction is at her devotion. The 13 cipher passages of f. 157 are read as Forbes prints them.

reading_review.note: Forbes, A Full View ii (1741), printed from the original with the deciphered words in italic; the cipher passages of Add MS 4136 aligned one to one with the italic stretches and checked on the glyphs with key R9261 (no01-no23_reread_log.md). Forbes ii 287-289; all 13 passages checked. Not transcribed before. Verified word by word 22 Oct 2026 (verify2_smith_align.py: reading aligned with Forbes's print, the source; OCR garbles checked on a second OCR): 0 words bracketed, 0 replaced; 0.968 clean on the body (unchanged).

texts.label: No. 02, Smith to Cecil, Paris, 27 Jan 1562/3 (R9249, f. 158)
texts.summary: Sir Thomas Smith to Cecil, Paris, 27 Jan 1562/3: the ciphered passages as Patrick Forbes copied them into his deciphering file (Add MS 4136), deciphered with Smith's key R9261 (all 32 passages; checked against Forbes ii 315-18). In decipher_A.md, Letter 1: glyphs and plaintext per passage.

reading_review.note: decipher_A.md Letter 1: 32 passages that read as English phrases and whole sentences (the rendering of Tankerville; one to be named on the other side with the Admiral; Monsieur Danville to come over into England) and align word for word with Forbes's print, which supplies the clear text between them.

texts.label: No. 03, Smith to Cecil, Blois, 7 Mar 1562/3 (R9252, ff. 163-4)
texts.summary: Smith to Cecil, Blois, 7 Mar 1562/3 (Forbes ii 350-351): the Guise's death has brought the French "even into my lap"; musters and captains, have all Normandy again this summer; no hostages or assurances for Calais, no quiet holding of Newhaven; the French confess their weakness and need of English friendship; Smith fears only the meddling of the Queen of Scots.

reading_review.note: Forbes, A Full View ii (1741), printed from the original with the deciphered words in italic; the cipher passages of Add MS 4136 aligned one to one with the italic stretches and checked on the glyphs with key R9261 (no01-no23_reread_log.md). texts.summary: Smith to the Queen, Blois, 12 Mar 1562/3 (Forbes ii 356-359): a Spanish packet intercepted at Trent reveals a Spanish-Imperial plan against France; the Admiral holds out on the peace terms and is looked for at court; the Spanish ambassador sounds Smith on Caen, Calais and the forfeit crowns; Condé is won over and will help drive the English out of France; the Emperor will denounce war over Metz, Toul and Verdun.

reading_review.note: Forbes, A Full View ii (1741), printed from the original with the deciphered words in italic; the cipher passages of Add MS 4136 aligned one to one with the italic stretches and checked on the glyphs with key R9261 (no01-no23_reread_log.md).
